Post loads to comments.

**Stimulus and Strategy:**  
Today's the day to lift heavy relative to your capacity. It's a session that demands full focus and attention on every set.
Check back on your most recent heavy front squat days from April 8 and July 7 to help navigate today's weight, or if you know a recent 1-rep-max front squat, aim for 75% or more of that number. If you did yesterday's workout, expect today's legs to reflect it — don't be discouraged if the weight feels lighter than usual. Start a new set every 3 minutes so you get plenty of rest between lifts; if you don't need that much recovery, go heavier, as long as your mechanics hold up. Newer athletes should lighten the load and prioritize quality reps over chasing heavier numbers.

**Intermediate option:**  
Same as Rx'd

**Beginner option:**   
Front squat **5-5-5-5-5-5-5** reps

On a 10-minute clock, complete:  
50 burpee pull-ups  
75 kettlebell swings  
Max burpee pull-ups in the remaining time

The pull-up bar should be 6 inches above the fingertips with arms extended overhead. Your score is the number of burpee pull-ups completed.

♀ 35-lb kettlebell  
♂ 53-lb kettlebell

Post your reps to the comments.

**Stimulus and Strategy:**  
Today's workout is a grind with a “rewarding” push at the end! Move through the first set of burpee pull-ups and kettlebell swings as quickly as possible, then, in the remaining time, perform as many burpee pull-ups as possible. Aim to complete the first set of burpee pull-ups in under 6 minutes. Choose a light kettlebell load that allows you to finish the swings in under 3:30 and in 2-3 sets. You should have at least 30 seconds to complete burpee pull-ups at the end of the workout. Some advanced athletes may have 3 minutes or more. 

**Intermediate option:**  
On a 10-minute clock, complete:
**35** burpee pull-ups  
**50** kettlebell swings  
Max burpee pull-ups in the remaining time

**Fingertips should touch the pull-up bar with arms extended overhead.** Your score is the number of burpee pull-ups completed.

♀ 35-lb kettlebell  
♂ 53-lb kettlebell

**Beginner option:**   
On a 10-minute clock, complete:  
**25 burpees**  
**25 jumping** pull-ups  
**50** kettlebell swings  
Max burpee **jumping** pull-ups in the remaining time

**Mid-forearm should touch the pull-up bar with arms extended overhead.** Your score is the number of **jumping** burpee pull-ups completed.

♀ **15**-lb kettlebell  
♂ **25**-lb kettlebell

21-15-9* reps for time of:  
Clean and jerks  
Echo bike calories

*Women complete 15-12-9 Echo bike calories.

Then, at 20 minutes:   
Build to a challenging power clean and jerk

♀ 65-lb barbell  
♂ 95-lb barbell

Post time and load to comments.

**Stimulus and Strategy:**  
Today's time domain tells you everything you need to know about this workout — it's fast! The light clean and jerks are meant to be completed in 1-3 sets across all rounds, with only brief rest breaks. Choose a load that lets you do at least 15 reps with smooth, high-quality movement. The bike is low skill, low repetition, but will challenge your respiratory system — find a calorie count that lets you hold a consistent moderate-to-hard effort. It should feel uncomfortable, but manageable. The set of 21 shouldn't take longer than 90 seconds. Today is about moving fast and consistently, with enough clarity and control to move the barbell well.

After the workout, feel free to take 10 minutes — or until your clock hits 20 minutes — to build to a challenging but not maximal power clean and jerk.

metadata.raw_content:
5 rounds for time of:  
200-meter run  
20 air squats  
20 push-ups  
20 lunges

Post time to comments.

**Stimulus and Strategy:**  
Today's workout is simple but challenging, regardless of your ability level. Some of you may have done it at the 2026 CrossFit Owners and Coaches Conference in the park. 

If you're proficient with the movement, challenge yourself to move at a very fast pace from the start and hang on. Expect the squat-and-lunge combination to fatigue your legs more than you might anticipate — these movements will make the runs harder too, so try to hold a steady, consistent pace. The push-ups may end up being the toughest part when performed with great mechanics and full range of motion. Be strategic about how you manage your reps: break them up before muscular failure sets in, and use short rest breaks.

**Intermediate option:**    
5 rounds for time of:  
200-meter run  
20 air squats  
**10** push-ups  
20 lunges

**Beginner option:**   
5 rounds for time of:  
200-meter run  
**10** air squats  
**10** push-ups **from the knees**  
**10** lunges

**Resources:**  
[Running | Falling Forward](https://youtu.be/zSrMZRh3ymk)  
[The Air Squat](https://www.crossfit.com/essentials/the-air-squat)
